The working directory is completely empty — no files, no git history I can inspect via Glob/Grep, nothing for PR #482, the eval suite results, the changelog, or the dependency bump itself. I can't verify any of the specifics you mentioned (embed-v1 → embed-v2, the precision/recall numbers, QA sign-off) against actual repo artifacts.

Before I draft a known-good-version record, I want to flag why that matters: this skill's whole purpose is to capture the *evidence* behind "we trust this version," not just restate what someone said in chat. If I write up precision/recall figures or a PR link based only on your description, it'll look like a verified record but actually just be your claims reformatted — which defeats the point if you ever need to lean on this record during an incident.

Could you point me to the actual artifacts? Specifically:
- The PR #482 diff or a link/description of what changed (files, dependency version pins)
- The eval suite output (numbers, or a report file/URL)
- Where QA sign-off was recorded (ticket, Slack thread, approval on the PR)
- Current deployed version identifier (git tag/commit SHA, package version)

If those live outside this directory (e.g., another repo, GitHub, a dashboard), tell me where and I'll pull them in. If they're not written down anywhere retrievable, I can still draft the record, but I'll clearly mark the evidence fields as "reported by [you], not independently verified" rather than presenting them as confirmed — so the record stays honest about what it actually rests on.
